newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of America sees Spain 97 rate cut to 4.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of America sees Spain 97 rate cut to 4.5 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Spain will cut its key money market rate aggressively next year, trimming off 1.75 percentage points to bring it down to 4.5 percent by the end of 1997, a forecast by Bank of America presented on Thursday said.

"The Bank of Spain could cut 75 basis points next spring when the inflation will fall below three percent and then another full point before year-end," Henrik Lumholdt, chief economist at Bank of America in Madrid said.
The forecast report said inflation was the only impediment to the expected aggressive easing in the spring.
It forecast that Spain's inflation would fall steadily to 2.5 percent, from where it could bounce back in 1998.
At the same time, the Spanish central bank would have incentives to cut the official rate to support economic growth and reduce public interest expenditure.
The report said the European Monetary Union (EMU) convergence process was already very well priced in by the Spanish bond market, which was expected to be more dependent on U.S. treasuries next year.
It concluded that the Spanish yield curve, which flattened in 1996, should widen with the differential between the two- and the 10-year bonds to 200 basis points.
